text: Horacio Coppola (31 July 1906 – 18 June 2012) was an Argentine photographer and filmmaker, and the husband of the German photographer Grete Stern. Born in Buenos Aires, he was the youngest of 10 children; his Italian immigrant parents were well off, and he studied art, music, law, and languages. He began taking photographs around the age of 20. In the 1920s and ’30s, he traveled to Europe, where photography was emerging as an art form, characterized by unusual angles and cropping. He met Grete Stern in Germany and later worked in London, taking portraits of famous artists and contributing to a book about Mesopotamian artifacts in the Louvre and the British Museum. In 1936, he and Stern returned to Argentina, where he was commissioned to photograph Buenos Aires for its 400th anniversary, producing streetscapes that depicted the city’s romance, vitality, and squalor. The couple had a daughter, Silvia, and a son, Andres, and later divorced. In 1959, Coppola married Raquel Palomeque, a pianist. He authored the photographs featured in the first edition of "Evaristo Carriego" (biography) (1930) by Jorge Luis Borges and was one of the pioneering Argentine photographers and a key figure in Modernism. He studied at the Bauhaus during the 1930s. Coppola was awarded the title of "Illustrious Citizen of Buenos Aires" and, at the age of 100, had a retrospective exhibit at the Malba Museum in Buenos Aires.
